relationships.scope: Extends the September 2017 approach (select from the High Court panel where the court/tribunal is in the same place, otherwise a fresh local panel) to CAT, consumer fora and lower courts.

limitations: This concerns EPFO's own panel advocates and legal practitioners, not EPF members' legal remedies. Fee amounts are in tables in the originals and are not summarised here; read the tables for the court and type of work.

The January 2012 circular tells offices to regulate fees under the Law Ministry's revised structure "with effect from 1.9.2011", while the enclosed Law Ministry OM is dated 18 September 2011 and says "immediate effect". The EPFO circular's own wording is recorded as the effective date; the difference is not resolved here.
The 2017 circular states no commencement date, so none is recorded. The 2017 and 2026 fee links are candidate links (target unverified) because neither names the earlier EPFO circular.

The 7 September 2017 circular follows the Gazette notification of 26 May 2017 merging EPF Appellate Tribunals into Central Government Industrial Tribunals; the policy on empanelment for the Supreme Court and CAT Principal Bench panel year 2026-29 (order of 29 July 2026) is not included because it is a list of named advocates.

The 2017 fee circular is listed twice on the issuer's site under the same number and date (two file names); one copy is used. The 16 May 2014 guidelines and earlier fee circulars (1999, 2008, 2011 OMs) are not in this collection except as enclosed texts.
Zonal empanelment notices and RTI replies naming advocates are not covered.
PDFs were read from the issuer mirror on 3 November 2026 because the public site returned 404 for these paths that day; recorded SHA-256 values apply to those files. Scanned pages are OCR.
